definition: A correlation coefficient is a number between -1 and +1 that measures how strongly two data series move in relation to each other.
core_idea: A value of +1 means the two series move identically together, -1 means they move exactly opposite (one rises as the other falls), and 0 means there is no discernible relationship between the two series' movements.
key_points: -1 = perfect inverse relationship (one rises as the other falls).
0 = no relationship; the two series move up and down randomly relative to each other, sometimes together and sometimes opposed.
relationships: Feeds into hedge selection and correlation-based valuation, but see the hedging caveat below.
trading_implications: Used to identify candidate price series (e.g., a proxy hub) for hedging or relative-value analysis.
caveats: A correlation coefficient describes co-movement, not whether the absolute price levels are close or trending the same direction over time.
